definitions.gloss: to write in cursive; to write loosely or roughly
definitions.explanation: To write characters in a simplified, flowing style rather than in their standard printed form. Can refer to intentional calligraphic cursive or to careless, hard-to-read handwriting.

examples.japanese: ⟦{漢字|かんじ}→漢字：09480_kanji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{崩|くず}して⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: To write kanji in cursive style.

examples.japanese: {書|か}き{崩|くず}した⟦{字|じ}→字：01606_ji⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧にくい。
examples.english: Loosely written characters are hard to read.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{書|か}き{崩|くず}して⟦あって→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{何|なに}→何：00498_nani⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{書|か}いてある→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦{分|わ}からなかった→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather's letter was written in such a loose hand that I couldn't tell what it said.

notes:
FORMS:
⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧ (to write) + ⟦{崩|くず}す→崩す：03919_kuzusu⟧ (to break down, to simplify). Literally 'to break down the writing,' meaning to simplify character strokes.

USAGE:
In calligraphy, {書|か}き{崩|くず}す can be a positive term describing artistic cursive (⟦{草書|そうしょ}→草書：19196_sousho⟧ or ⟦{行書|ぎょうしょ}→行書：19195_gyousho⟧ style). In everyday contexts, it often describes handwriting that is too loose or messy to read easily.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{字|じ}→字：01606_ji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{崩|くず}す (to write characters loosely)
- {書|か}き{崩|くず}した⟦{文字|もじ}→文字：03632_moji⟧ (loosely written characters)
- ⟦{達筆|たっぴつ}→達筆：26860_tappitsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{書|か}き{崩|くず}して⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧ (written in skilled cursive)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {崩|くず}し{字|じ}: cursive characters — the noun form for characters written in simplified style
